reading.body:
DartPoints Shreveport publishes 2.2 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that is roughly 55 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it is roughly 220 racks. The operator has not published power density targets, redundancy tier, or cooling architecture on the spec page this site read, so no further translation is possible from the data in hand.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no qualification statements can be made about what compliance regimes the campus satisfies.

Within Louisiana, this site holds four mapped facilities, three of which publish a megawatt figure, totaling 7.7 MW across those three. DartPoints Shreveport contributes 2.2 MW of that total, ranking third among facilities with published capacity in the state. Louisiana's published data center footprint, as this site has read it, is small: 7.7 MW across three facilities is a thin base for AI workloads at scale, and this campus, at roughly 29 percent of that published state total, represents a regional edge presence rather than a concentration of AI compute.
